newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai to investigate rumours on stock market.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai to investigate rumours on stock market.

text.p: The Shanghai securities authorities will investigate rumours that led the stock market to plunge on Wednesday, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.

Shanghai's A index closed down 62.766 points or 5.85 percent to 1009.351 points on Wednesday on rumours, including one that securities authorities would shortly announce new measures to crack down on trading on credit and a new quota for share issues which would quicken the pace of market expansion.
"Yesterday the Shanghai stock market plunged in an abnormal way, with various rumours spreading on the market and depressing investor confidence," the newspaper said.
"The Shanghai Securities Administration Office has said that it will severely punish those who spread rumours and manipulated the markets on rumours," the newspaper said.
The newspaper urged investors to resist rumours and be calm no matter what kinds of rumours spread on the market.

"It is normal that there will be rumours on securities markets but a maturing market should not fluctuate sharply on the influence of rumours," the newspaper said. "If investors trade stocks on rumours, they will only hurt themselves."

The newspaper said China's national economy was good this year, the central government was supporting the stock market and the performance of listed firms was improving. Investors should have enough confidence, it said.
Despite the reassurance, Shanghai's A share index fell 8.075 points or 0.8 percent to 1001.276 by mid-morning on Thursday.
